submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the token that spells out a personal name - a given name (' Sarah', ' David', ' Pete'), a surname (' Wilson', ' Fernandez'), or an interior BPE fragment or initial of one ('airo' inside ' Nairobi', 'ian' in ' Maximilian', a byline ' H') - and the peak is set jointly by the token's name-likeness and by whether the preceding words make a person the expected referent (after 'by', 'and', 'said', 'named' or a title such as 'Dr'/'author' real names reach 1.4-2.5; in a neutral sentence the same name reaches only 0.4-0.9). It reads exactly 0.00 on organisation/brand names ('Microsoft', 'Google', 'IBM', 'NATO', 'Harvard') in every plain frame and only about 0.9 when a title forces a person reading ('Dr Microsoft'), 0.00 on lowercase common nouns and on place names in place frames ('The capital of France is Paris/Madrid'), about 0.2 when a determiner immediately precedes the name ('the Sarah'), and 0.00 on every token of a name that opens the text ('Sarah arrived at the office early').

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The software giant Microsoft reported record profits this quarter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hypothesis says organisation and brand names read exactly 0.00 in every plain frame, so 'Microsoft' after a common noun in a financial sentence must not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She bought an Apple laptop and a Samsung phone at the mall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A brand name sits immediately after ' and', the very cue the hypothesis says lifts real personal names, but this is a plain shopping frame where it says brand names still read 0.00.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The capital of Japan is Tokyo, though many assume it is Kyoto.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Place name in a classic place frame of the type the hypothesis names explicitly ('The capital of France is Paris'), which it says reads 0.00 even though 'Tokyo' appears in a top-activating example.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Flights from London to Madrid and Rome were cancelled because of the storm.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Place name directly after ' and' in a transport list, testing whether the cue token alone or the claimed person-expected-referent condition drives the peak; the hypothesis predicts 0.00 for place names in place frames.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She accepted the award with grace and thanked the committee.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lowercase common noun that is a given name only when capitalised, so the hypothesis predicts 0.00 on this token even though 'and' precedes the phrase.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Please mark the envelope clearly before you mail it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Lowercase 'mark' as a verb, the given name 'Mark' in another casing and sense, which the hypothesis says reads 0.00 because the token is a lowercase common noun rather than a name.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In the novel, the Sarah character never appears in person.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A determiner immediately precedes the name, the case the hypothesis quantifies at only about 0.2, far below its 1.4-2.5 person-cue band.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Wilson's theorem states that for any prime p, (p-1)! is congruent to -1.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A personal surname opens the text, the position the hypothesis says reads 0.00 on every token of a name that opens the text.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: A spokesperson for NATO declined to comment on the reports.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An acronym organisation in a plain frame, one of the exact strings the hypothesis lists as reading 0.00.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She opened the parcel and found the letters inside.
adversarial_test_results.detail: No name token at all but the same 'opened the' verb-plus-determiner shape as a top example, testing whether the hypothesis's peak on 'the' is a delimiter artifact rather than the claimed name effect.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The gallery confirmed that the portrait was painted by Fernandez in 1893.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Surname after 'by' in an art-world frame, a context unlike the examples, which the hypothesis predicts reaches 1.4-2.5.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The keynote was delivered by Dr. Okafor, who had flown in from Lagos.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A title precedes an unseen surname, which the hypothesis says creates a person referent and lifts the name token into its 1.4-2.5 band.
Personal name after 'by' inside a code comment, a cross-genre context the hypothesis should generalise to if it tracks names rather than the scan corpus's phrasing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her parents decided to name the baby Amelia after her grandmother.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase of the naming cue using the verb 'name' introducing a given name, which the hypothesis says still makes a person the expected referent and so fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Filed by R. Chaudhary, the story appeared on page one.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A byline initial before a surname, the exact ' H'-style case the hypothesis lists as an activating token.

The foreman wrote that down, finished the count, and handed the sheet to the young woman waiting by the door. "Get this to the office before the bank closes," he told her.
